record_types.GEN: genealogy, influence, anti-genealogy, lost-lineage, scene, or event record
record_types.PAT: recurring pattern / failure mode / epistemic pattern
record_types.CLA: claim record that may be supported, qualified, or defeated by other records
record_types.INF: source infrastructure / reporting system / registry / database / recommendation tracking system record
record_types.MET: meta-research audit record: empirical study of missingness, reporting bias, reproducibility, reversal, de-adoption, or evidence-production mechanisms
record_types.FACET: not a promoted record type; a cross-cutting factor axis used to classify records without proliferating record types

status_tokens.seed_mention: mentioned in the seed document only; not a verified record
status_tokens.candidate: accepted as a candidate target for source acquisition
status_tokens.source_located: at least one source located but not extracted
status_tokens.primary_source_backed: primary source exists and has been captured or linked with permanence metadata
status_tokens.extracted: key fields extracted into a record shell
status_tokens.reviewed: second pass checked fields, status, and source dependence
status_tokens.synthesized: linked to neighboring records and lessons
status_tokens.contested: material disagreement remains and is explicitly tracked
status_tokens.superseded: record remains historically useful but current status changed
status_tokens.retired: candidate or claim should no longer be treated as active
status_tokens.promoted_record_primary_source_backed_on: A record sourced from at least one primary or official source and extracted into fields, but not yet second-pass reviewed or fully synthesized.
status_tokens.pattern_candidate_multi_case_source_back: A provisional pattern candidate supported by multiple records, retained with caveats and not yet admitted as a stable theory.
status_tokens.promoted_record_genealogy_infrastructure: A genealogy infrastructure record promoted from official/institutional source extraction; no unsourced graph import implied.
status_tokens.promoted_record_scene_source_backed_one_: A bounded scene/event record with sources, typed relations, and caveats; not a full history.
status_tokens.promoted_record_program_audit_negative_r: A record where a formal evaluator/audit report narrows or defeats a broad program promise under explicit criteria.
status_tokens.promoted_record_anti_genealogy_audit_sce: A record for a response-against/evaluator scene where criticism, mandate, response, and downstream effects must be separated.
status_tokens.pattern_candidate_program_audit_source_b: A provisional pattern about program audits and accountable scope; requires controls and consequence records.
status_tokens.promoted_record_source_infrastructure_on: A source-backed infrastructure record describing a reporting, registry, database, or recommendation-tracking system; not an effectiveness claim.
status_tokens.pattern_candidate_infrastructure_source_: A provisional pattern candidate derived from infrastructure records; it names a design family without claiming outcome effectiveness or frequency.
status_tokens.foundation_audited_and_factored_not_seco: A foundation surface has been structurally audited and factored, while factual records remain mostly one-pass reviewed.
status_tokens.schema_debt_identified: The object is coherent enough to use but needs schema normalization or stricter validation before scale.

evidence_classes.primary_official: official report, registry record, court record, regulator report, archived primary data, preregistration, original publication
evidence_classes.primary_participant: memoir, interview, lab notebook, correspondence, public statement by participant
evidence_classes.journalistic: reported account requiring corroboration for record promotion
evidence_classes.informal: blog, forum, social post, conference slide, repository note; useful but fragile
evidence_classes.seed_only: this archive seed or prior-art note only; never enough for a factual record
evidence_classes.official_program_briefing: Official program description from the operating institution.
evidence_classes.official_confidentiality_policy: Official policy page describing confidentiality, de-identification, or reporting protections.

link_types.qualifies: record narrows or limits another claim
link_types.contradicts: record directly conflicts with another claim
link_types.replicates: record attempts direct or conceptual replication
link_types.supports: record supports another claim or synthesis
link_types.defeats: record undercuts evidential authority of another record
link_types.recurs_with: shares a failure pattern with another record
link_types.commissioned_evaluation: a body commissions a report/evaluation of a field or program
link_types.field_naming: a scene/source helps name or define a field, without implying sole origin
link_types.program_audit: a formal evaluator assesses a research or engineering program under criteria
link_types.evidence_ref: Future normalized claim-support reference with explicit ref_kind; introduced because source_id is currently overloaded for record-to-record support in pattern claims.
link_types.claim_supported_by_ref: Graph edge from claim to typed evidence reference target.
link_types.pattern_candidate_currently_supported_by: Graph edge from pattern candidate to support record, candidate-level only.

source_permanence_tokens.doi_or_registry: durable identifier exists but content may still move
source_permanence_tokens.local_hash_only: archive has hash/provenance but not content
source_permanence_tokens.private_or_sensitive: not copied; handling constrained by ethics or law

sensitivity_classes.low: ordinary scholarly correction or technical record
sensitivity_classes.medium: reputation, institutional failure, or contested scholarly implications
sensitivity_classes.high: death, survivor/family trauma, medical harm, stigmatized groups, security, or legal exposure
sensitivity_classes.restricted: private, confidential, personally identifying, or ethically constrained material

core_project_terms.denominator_graph: A linked representation of attempts, sources, claims, failures, corrections, transmission paths, and practice lag, designed to reveal what positive-result canons omit.
core_project_terms.failure_literacy: The ability to reason with nulls, reversals, non-replications, engineering failures, source fragility, and status change without blame spectacle or naive cynicism.
core_project_terms.practice_lag: A gap between changed evidence/literature status and changed real-world practice, policy, textbook, clinical, engineering, or product behavior.
core_project_terms.status_history: A time-indexed sequence of epistemic states for a claim, rather than a single final verdict.
core_project_terms.earned_pattern: A pattern record promoted only after multiple sourced records support recurrence.
core_project_terms.numeric_assumption_mismatch: A failure mode in which units, numeric range, time precision, or representation validity assumptions cross a boundary where they no longer hold.
core_project_terms.signal_commons: A reporting or database infrastructure that turns weak, private, or identity-sensitive signals into shared safety knowledge under privacy and action-routing constraints.
core_project_terms.factor_axis: A dimension that can cut across record types, such as evidence surface, status motion, correction surface, transmission edge, harm/sensitivity, denominator visibility, or pattern maturity.
core_project_terms.locator_debt: A claim or source whose current locator is a search snippet, vague page pointer, or non-stable prose reference rather than a durable page/line/section locator.
core_project_terms.schema_closure: The state where schemas validate the records they are supposed to govern and lint enforces that validation.
core_project_terms.red_team_controls: Mandatory pattern-candidate scaffold naming positive controls, negative controls, counterexamples to seek, rollback triggers, and maturity gates.
core_project_terms.graph_edge_surface: A normalized read surface over records, sources, claims, links, and pattern support; useful for querying but not yet canonical.

claim_support_terms.evidence_refs: Canonical claim-support field introduced in rev0016. Each ref has ref_id, ref_kind, support_role, confidence, and optional locator/support_type.
claim_support_terms.source_support: Legacy field removed from promoted record claims in rev0016 because it overloaded source_id and record_id.
claim_support_terms.sources_or_support: Legacy claim-ledger field removed in rev0016 in favor of evidence_refs.
claim_support_terms.support_role: Why the referenced object is being used: direct source support, supporting pattern record, infrastructure context, or self-scope/status support.
claim_support_terms.ref_kind: Controlled kind of referenced object: source, engineering_record, negative_result_record, replication_record, genealogy_record, infrastructure_record, metaresearch_record, pattern_record, or claim.
